name: nlp_seq2seq_summarization
title: A T5 summariser: Seq2SeqTrainer plus a hand-written beam-search generation pass scored with ROUGE
origin: hardening round 1, domain-nlp, 2026-09-13 - the seq2seq shape, and the generation loop nothing models
note: Three of the eight labels below miss for one shared reason: transformers.AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM is not in knowledge/other_tbl.py, so the T5 model carries no MODEL tag and no node, and model.generate() is in no knowledge table either, so the generation loop is not an evaluation region for any rule (findings NLP-06 and NLP-07).

expected.defect: the holdout is cut with no seed=
expected.why: datasets.Dataset.train_test_split shuffles by default, so the 5% held out changes on every run and two ROUGE numbers from this script are not comparable

expected.defect: the Seq2SeqTrainer is given no eval_dataset and the arguments set no evaluation strategy
expected.why: predict_with_generate=True is set and never used, so two epochs of fine-tuning run with nothing scored on held-out data

expected.defect: the resume path calls torch.load with neither weights_only= nor map_location=
expected.why: it unpickles arbitrary objects and fails on a machine without the device the checkpoint was written on

expected.defect: the generation loader shuffles the holdout
expected.why: the decoded summaries come back in a different order every run, so the per-article comparison the report table is built on is wrong

expected.defect: the evaluation moves the model to CUDA outright with no torch.cuda.is_available() anywhere in the workspace
expected.why: the script cannot run on a CPU-only machine, which is where a summarisation eval is usually re-run

expected.defect: the generation pass never calls model.eval()
expected.why: T5 keeps its dropout active during decoding, so every beam is drawn through a randomly perturbed model and the ROUGE printed is both wrong and irreproducible

expected.defect: the generation loop is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: beam search keeps an autograd graph for every decoding step of every beam, which is the commonest out-of-memory in a summarisation evaluation

expected.defect: the whole module is pickled rather than model.state_dict()
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path and stops loading the moment transformers changes the class
the holdout, the fine-tune and the dropout during decoding all move between runs

forbidden.why: Seq2SeqTrainer owns the optimisation loop; no hand-written update exists in this project
no backward() is written anywhere here
the only DataLoader in this project is the generation loader; the training batches are the Trainer's
ROUGE is computed over decoded strings; no class metric is involved
no ranking metric appears in this project
no loss is constructed here at all - the T5 head computes its own
no nn.Module subclass is defined in this project
no submodule container is built here

unsupported.defect: the collator pads the label ids with -100 so the loss can ignore them; decoding them with batch_decode raises or produces garbage references, so the ROUGE is computed against the wrong strings
unsupported.why: no rule models the -100/pad-id convention on a seq2seq label tensor

unsupported.defect: targets are truncated to 96 tokens while generation_max_length is the same 96, so any reference longer than the cap is silently cut and the model is trained never to finish a summary
unsupported.why: no rule compares a truncation length with a generation length

unsupported.defect: the evaluation reuses the fine-tuned model in memory rather than reloading the checkpoint it will ship, so a serialisation bug in torch.save on line 45 is invisible to the number being reported
unsupported.why: MLV902 is a later-tier rule and covers tokenizer/checkpoint identifier mismatch, not train/serve object identity
